observations: Two used automatic transmission gearboxes are shown, one on top of the other.
The gearboxes are in a workshop or storage area with other engine components.
The top gearbox has a large central hub with multiple bolts and a visible oil filler cap.
The bottom gearbox has a similar central hub and a pink marking on the oil filler cap.
The gearboxes have numerous hoses, wiring harnesses, and mechanical components attached.
The gearboxes appear dirty and used, consistent with being stored for parts.
No brand names, model numbers, or technical specifications are visible on the gearboxes.

claims.evidence: No manual gearbox is shown in the photos.
No Toyota Corolla is shown in the photos.
No Toyota Carry or Hillux is shown in the photos.

risks.risk: The gearbox may be seized, stripped, or have internal mechanical failure.
risks.proof: A video showing the gearbox being manually shifted through all gears.

risks.risk: The gearbox may be a generic or third-party part rather than a genuine Toyota part.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's identification plate (usually on the housing or a metal plate).

risks.risk: The gearbox may be missing essential components like the clutch assembly or the oil pump.
risks.proof: A photo of the complete gearbox with all internal components installed.
risks.if_unproven: as a bare gearbox with missing clutch and pump

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the manufacturer's identification plate on the gearbox housing.
Video of the gearbox being shifted through all gears to check for internal damage.
Photo of the clutch assembly and oil pump to check for missing parts.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
